findings.title: Restore or explicitly revise whether the severed refuge closes the breach.
blueprintEvidence: round1 acts[2].arcs[1].dnaHint: severed refuge "closes its breach".

findings.reason: The new care distinction is useful, but replacing both operative outcome passages removed the previous explicit guarantee that refuge planting also seals the central breach. Readers can now infer that only joined restoration closes it, or import the earlier meaning; this changes a material choice consequence unintentionally if upkeep was the only intended change.
findings.recommendation: Add a short clause to the refuge outcome confirming that it also closes the central breach, if retaining the earlier rule. If the author intentionally changes that effect, state the new consequence plainly and align all ending descriptions before the player chooses.
findings.mitigation: The act turning point still contrasts restoration with smaller refuge, and the trunk description broadly permits planting to close the breach. Neither explicitly fixes the refuge effect, although a GM may infer the old rule.
findings.confidence: High that explicit refuge breach closure was removed from both operative passages; medium that a model would misinterpret it.

findings.title: Refuge planting no longer explicitly closes the central breach
findings.basis: §9.1 consistency of the world (◐ secondary); §8.4 consequences knowable before action (◐ secondary).

blueprintEvidence.quote: planting at the trunk restores surviving branches and seals the central breach.
Cutting outward roots first concentrates the reserve into a durable local refuge
while ending the old star-road and leaving distant dark reaches unsafe.

findings.reason: Round one explicitly said severed refuge also seals the breach in both the final arc hint and outcome rule. Round two replaces both passages: only the joined-root clause now promises closure. A durable local canopy might repel feeders without closing their source, so the intended central outcome has become ambiguous exactly when the player must compare options.
findings.recommendation: If the intended consequence remains as in round one, explicitly restore central breach closure to the severed-refuge outcome in rule and final hint. If deliberately changing it, state the open-breach consequence and its implications consistently; do not let it be decided after the choice.
findings.mitigation: The trunk description still says planting here can close the breach, and the first review established both options doing so. A small wording restoration fixes this; no broader plot change needed.
findings.confidence: High about lost explicit clauses across round comparison; medium about runtime inference. This is ambiguity introduced by editing, not observed model failure.

reviewers.uncertainty: This is private-canon review, not a corpus judgment of rhythm, exposition or experienced delight. No runtime claims.
